subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Second-Life Batteries
description: A fast breakdown of Second-Life Batteries for builders.

hook.text: When an EV battery drops below 80 percent capacity, it's no longer great for driving—but far from dead.

buildup.text: These retired packs still hold huge amounts of energy, perfect for less demanding applications.

discovery.text: Old EV batteries are being repurposed as stationary storage for solar panels and grid backup.

twist.text: Nissan and BMW already run projects where retired car batteries power buildings and stabilize grids.

climax.text: Second-life use could extend the total value of each battery by a decade before recycling is needed.

punchline.text: An EV battery's second career might last longer than its first.

quiz.question: What happens to EV batteries when they drop below 80% capacity?
options: They can be reused for stationary energy storage

details.summary: When EV batteries degrade to roughly 80 percent capacity, they are no longer ideal for driving but can serve a second life as stationary energy storage for homes, businesses, and power grids.
details.whyItMatters: Second-life applications extend the useful lifespan of expensive battery packs by a decade or more, improving the economics and environmental footprint of electric vehicle ownership.
takeaways: Retired EV packs still hold 70 to 80 percent of their original capacity
They can store solar energy or stabilize the power grid
Second life delays recycling and maximizes resource utilization

faq.question: How long can a second-life battery last in stationary storage?
faq.answer: With gentler charge and discharge cycles than vehicular use, second-life batteries can often last an additional 5 to 10 years in stationary applications before they need to be recycled.

faq.question: Is it cheaper to use second-life EV batteries than new ones for storage?
faq.answer: Yes. Repurposed EV batteries cost significantly less than new cells because the manufacturing cost has already been absorbed. This makes them attractive for budget-conscious grid and home storage projects.
